digest.lead: Major security news today as reports surface that the NSA is using Anthropic's Mythos model for cyber operations, while Anthropic releases new open-source vulnerability discovery tools.
digest.summary: Claude Code gets version management features and plugin controls, while the community discusses AI safety concerns and cost-aware agent frameworks.

stories.headline: NSA Using Anthropic's Mythos Model for Cyber Operations
stories.summary: Reports indicate the NSA is utilizing Anthropic's Mythos model for cyber attack operations [1]. The news has generated significant discussion in the tech community about the implications of AI models being used for offensive cyber capabilities.
stories.impact: This raises important questions about AI governance and the use of commercial AI models by government agencies for offensive capabilities, potentially affecting Anthropic's reputation and regulatory landscape.

sources.title: NSA using Anthropic's Mythos for cyber attacks

stories.headline: Anthropic Calls for Global AI Development Pause Over Self-Improvement Risks
stories.summary: Anthropic has urged a global pause in AI development, specifically flagging concerns about AI systems achieving 'self-improvement' capabilities [1]. The announcement has received mixed reception in the tech community with limited engagement compared to other AI safety discussions.
stories.impact: This positions Anthropic as taking a cautious stance on AI safety, potentially influencing industry discussions about responsible AI development timelines and regulatory approaches.

sources.title: Anthropic Urges Global Pause in AI Development, Flags 'Self-Improvement' Risk

stories.headline: Anthropic Releases Open-Source AI Vulnerability Discovery Framework
stories.summary: Anthropic has open-sourced a framework for AI-powered vulnerability discovery, generating substantial community interest [1]. The release appears to be part of Anthropic's broader security research initiatives and has attracted significant developer attention.
stories.impact: This provides security researchers and developers with new tools for automated vulnerability discovery, potentially improving software security practices across the industry.

sources.title: Anthropic's open-source framework for AI-powered vulnerability discovery

stories.headline: Claude Code Adds Version Management and Plugin Controls
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.163 introduces enterprise-friendly version management with `requiredMinimumVersion` and `requiredMaximumVersion` settings that prevent startup outside allowed ranges [1]. The update also adds a `/plugin list` command with filtering options and a convenient copy shortcut for `/btw` responses [1]. A minor bug fix release (v2.1.165) followed shortly after [2].
key_points: New version enforcement prevents Claude Code from starting outside approved version ranges
Plugin management improved with list command and enable/disable filters
Enhanced clipboard integration for `/btw` responses with preserved formatting
stories.impact: These updates primarily benefit enterprise teams managing Claude Code deployments at scale, providing better version control and plugin oversight for IT administrators.

stories.headline: Cost.dev Launches Cost-Aware AI Agent Framework
stories.summary: Y Combinator-backed Cost.dev has launched a framework designed to make AI agents more cost-aware and cheaper to operate [1]. The project is gaining attention from developers looking to optimize their AI agent deployment costs.
stories.impact: This addresses a growing concern among developers deploying AI agents at scale, potentially reducing operational costs for teams using Claude and other models in production workflows.

stories.headline: Use /plugin list command to manage Claude Code plugins
stories.summary: The new /plugin list command helps you track which plugins are installed and their status. You can filter to see only enabled or disabled plugins, making plugin management much easier.
actionable_steps: Type `/plugin list` in Claude Code to see all installed plugins
Use `/plugin list --enabled` to see only active plugins
Use `/plugin list --disabled` to see only inactive plugins

stories.headline: Set up MCP servers to extend Claude's capabilities
stories.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers allow Claude to connect to external services like databases, APIs, and monitoring tools. This dramatically expands what Claude can do beyond just code editing.
actionable_steps: Create or locate a `.mcp.json` file in your project
Add server configuration with connection details
Install the MCP server using Claude Code's MCP management
Verify the connection and test available tools

stories.headline: Organize project rules using .claude/rules/ directory structure
stories.summary: The .claude/rules/ directory lets you break down complex project instructions into organized, manageable files. This makes it easier to maintain large codebases and share specific rules across multiple projects.
actionable_steps: Create a .claude/rules/ directory in your project root
Split your CLAUDE.md instructions into focused rule files (e.g., coding-style.md, testing.md)
Use symlinks to share common rules across multiple projects
Reference rule files from your main CLAUDE.md using import statements

stories.headline: Use claude project purge to clean up Claude Code project state
stories.summary: The new purge command removes all Claude Code artifacts for a project including transcripts, tasks, file history, and config entries. This is useful for cleaning up projects or starting fresh without manual file deletion.
actionable_steps: Run 'claude project purge [path]' to delete all Claude Code state for a project
Use '--dry-run' flag first to preview what will be deleted
Add '-y' or '--yes' to skip confirmation prompts, or '-i' for interactive mode

stories.headline: Use terminalSequence field to enable desktop notifications from Claude Code hooks
stories.summary: The terminalSequence field allows Claude Code hooks to emit desktop notifications, window titles, and terminal bells even when running without a controlling terminal. This is particularly useful for background processes or automated workflows that need to communicate status updates to users.
actionable_steps: Update your hook JSON output to include the terminalSequence field
Configure the field to emit the desired notification type (desktop notification, window title, or bell)
Test the hook in an environment without a controlling terminal to verify notifications work
